test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said, "I wish I had not wasted those years."

options.text: He said he wished he had not wasted those years.
He said he wished not to waste those years.
He said that he did not waste those years.
He wished that he would not waste those years.

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. He said he wished he had not wasted those years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in direct speech, where the speaker expresses a wish about something in the past.
 
• When converting such a sentence into indirect speech:
 
 
• The verb "wish" remains unchanged but is moved into the past tense.
 
• The past perfect tense ("had not wasted") remains the same because the situation being described refers to a hypothetical regret about the past.
 
 
 
• Option 1 accurately conveys this transformation, as it maintains the past perfect tense and appropriately reflects the speaker's regret.
 
• Options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect because they either change the meaning, tense, or structure of the original sentence.

Correct sentence: *He said he wished he had not wasted those years.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• Direct speech quotes the speaker's exact words, e.g., "I wish I had not wasted those years."
 
• Indirect speech reports what the speaker said without quoting directly, e.g., He said he wished he had not wasted those years.
 
 
 
• **When reporting wishes about the past:**
 
 
• The verb "wish" is usually followed by the past perfect tense to express regret about a past situation.
 
• Example: "I wish I had studied more." → She said she wished she had studied more.
